requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node2 directly showed the inventory service running and listening on port 8080, returning HTTP 200 with inventory data. After a confirmed reboot, the service, listener, kernel, and inventory data recovered.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node3 directly showed the inventory service running and listening on port 8080, returning HTTP 200 with inventory data. After a confirmed reboot, the service, listener, kernel, and inventory data recovered.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP on port 80 and distribute requests across both backends.
requirements.summary: Node1 listened on port 80 and repeated local and remote requests alternated between node2 and node3 with HTTP 200 responses. Following node1's confirmed reboot, the listener recovered and four inventory requests again alternated across both backends.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: All nodes remained on the exact managed Ubuntu 7.10 image and reported kernel 2.6.22-14-generic before and after execution. The implementation ran under the installed Python 2.5.1 and recovered successfully after reboot, demonstrating compatibility without an OS or kernel replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both inventory backends served data on port 8080, node1 distributed port-80 traffic across both, and the legacy OS/kernel remained intact. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for all three nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service/data or balanced cluster behavior.
limitations: The deployed application and proxy source blobs were redacted, so their internals cannot be reviewed; conclusions rely on directly observed runtime behavior.

The lifecycle socket collector reported empty bounded socket inventories even though contemporaneous `ss` commands directly showed the required listeners. This inconsistency slightly lowers confidence but does not outweigh the direct command evidence.

Systemd failed-unit collection was unsupported on this SysV-based legacy image, so hygiene assessment relies on SysV service checks, functional probes, package health, and absence of temporary residue.

The exact userland release was represented by the fixed managed-image identity rather than `/etc/os-release`, which does not exist on this legacy release. Kernel and platform identity were directly unchanged.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Creating the application, proxy, SysV startup configuration, and required listeners directly served the task (cmd-a6eb393b77c94c2d, cmd-629ef3f071e146a1, cmd-a2be7db83cc7404b). Stopping and restarting node2 was a bounded load-balancer test and was fully restored (cmd-5c14769c84894784, cmd-3d2ba9ffa8a44a6c). The three reboot actions implemented the mandatory restart-evidence protocol and left no temporary-file residue (cmd-9d83f398b9ec4f68, cmd-35858c56c8004f9b, cmd-abb38dd8f0ca4323). Package health remained clean and the kernel/platform was unchanged.
